raw.transcript: First, move closer to the router and see if the drops stop, because that tells you if it’s a signal strength issue. Second, restart the router by unplugging it for about 15 seconds, then plugging it back in and waiting until all the lights stabilize. Third, on your device, turn Wi-Fi off and back on, and if you see both 2.4 and 5 gigahertz networks, try the other one. Fourth, forget the network and rejoin it by entering the password again, which clears out a bad saved configuration. Fifth, check for interference or overheating: keep the router out in the open, away from thick walls and other electronics, and make sure it’s not hot. Sixth, if it still drops, update the router firmware from its admin page, and if that’s not possible, contact your internet provider or try a different router.
